name: reference-dark-2026-09-03
method: rendered specimens rated side by side in a browser, in a dark console, by the reference reader. Contrast was bisected to a floor and a ceiling from a ladder of ratios; size, weight, line height and letter spacing were chosen from graded specimens; the hue rule came from a chip that passed the ratio and could not be read.

contrast.note: prose lives in the band. Semantic colours (state chips) are scanned rather than read; they are held to the floor, not the band, because forcing them into it breaks the state vocabulary for no gain.

hue.note: a contrast ratio is blind to hue. Text needs a background that differs in more than brightness: either the hues are this far apart, or the background is desaturated below this, so the ink's own chroma makes the edge.

type.note: light text on a dark ground blooms and reads heavier than it is; the compensation is lighter weight, not bolder. Zero letter spacing read as cramped and .22em as unreadable. Nothing below the floor, anywhere. Sizes in rem so a reader's own browser setting still counts.

taxes.all_caps: never for text a person reads; it removes the word shape a reader navigates by
taxes.monospace: identifiers, hashes, paths, timestamps and code only; prose in monospace loses its silhouette
taxes.note: each of the three costs legibility on its own. Stacked, they were the worst text on every surface measured.

tables.overflow: truncate with an ellipsis; a cell that is genuinely prose opts back in to wrapping by name
tables.wrap: break-word, never anywhere: anywhere also shrinks a column below its longest word and breaks identifiers mid-token
